title: 06 · Roadside board: Howl Hill Weekender
strengths: The most believable composite of the set: the print is perspective-matched to the board and multiplied, so the corrugated ridges show through the yellow, the eucalyptus shadow falls across 'HOWL', and the low sun stays on top of the ink
The photo is real, empty of people, and the caption is one white line on the tarmac; nothing else is added
The hero itself prints well: flat yellow and blue, hard shapes, a lineup ticker that runs off the board's edge like a real wrap
slop_signals: Two web buttons are printed on a billboard: 'GET TICKETS £89' and '▸ PLAY LINEUP' with button chrome and an offset shadow; a print would carry a URL or a price line, not controls
The feathered blur band across the shops behind the fence reads as a smudge rather than depth of field, because nothing else at that distance is blurred
fixes: Swap the two buttons for printed text in the same voice: 'TICKETS £89 · HOWLHILL.LIVE' and 'LINEUP ON THE BACK' (or a QR mark)
Replace the blur band with a 4 to 6 px blur applied to the whole far plane behind the fence, or crop 60 px off the right so the shop signs leave the frame

references.what: Golden-hour photograph with type; the light is the subject and the type sits inside it, which is what the board does
A product in real sunlight; the screen reads as paper because it takes the scene's light, the same multiply logic as our print
A flat yellow card over a photograph stays believable when the photo keeps its texture
Case-study tiles with work shown in photographed places; the register the poster plate belongs in

owner.said: Hide all 6: approved the round 4 audit's removals (mockups showing removed pieces, heroes repeating the product screens, a generic timer)

owner_history.said: when designs are bad, mockups will also be bad; work on them
